checks: When the maximum has multiplicity r≤d−1, the nonmaximal coordinate sum on the upper tail is less than δ/g, where g is the smallest positive gap. The density of those k=d+1−r coordinates has exponent r−1≥0 in the remaining barycentric mass, hence is bounded on the integration region. The tail is O(δ^k) with k≥2, so the ratio at m−δ equals m−δ+O(δ²)<m.

When r=d, the cap for a<t≤m is a vertex simplex with linear scale (t−a)/(m−a), including the entire simplex at m. The ratio t(m−a)/(t−a) has derivative −a(m−a)/(t−a)²<0. Thresholds at or below a have no positive mass, and thresholds above m give ratio t>m.
A strictly positive constant row has an atom at m and domain [m,∞), where the ratio is t. The only minimizer is m. These cases exhaust all maximum multiplicities for a strictly positive row.

For d=2 with heights (1,2,3), direct edge intercepts give upper-tail fraction δ²/2 near 3. For heights (1,2,2), the lower-cap fraction is (t−1)² for 1<t≤2 and the decreasing ratio has value 2 at the full threshold.
